title: Sell Mineral Rights in Level Green, PA
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights level green pa
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Level Green, PA
metaDescription: Level Green, a growing Westmoreland County suburb, still sits above wet-gas Marcellus acreage. See how growth affects mineral value here.
heroLead: Level Green has grown steadily as a Pittsburgh-area suburb, but the ground underneath its newer developments still carries the wet-gas Marcellus rights that came with the farmland it replaced.
intro: Watching Level Green fill in with new subdivisions over the past few decades, it's easy to forget that every one of those lots used to be part of a working farm, and every one of those old farms had a mineral history of its own. Some of those minerals were sold along with the surface when the developer bought in; plenty were reserved by the original farm family and are still theirs today, even though they may have no other connection to the neighborhood that replaced their land.

sections.heading: Suburban Growth Didn't Erase the Old Mineral Deeds
paragraphs: When a Westmoreland County farm gets sold for development, the sale deed either conveys the minerals along with the surface or reserves them, and that decision is recorded permanently regardless of what gets built afterward. We check the specific transaction that turned farmland into today's Level Green subdivisions to see which happened.

sections.heading: Wet-Gas Value Doesn't Care About Zoning
paragraphs: Mineral value is set by geology and drilling activity, not by whether the surface above it is residential or agricultural. Westmoreland's wet-gas window runs under Level Green the same as it runs under farmland twenty miles away, and horizontal drilling means a well doesn't need to sit directly under a subdivision to reach the gas beneath it.

sections.heading: What This Means If You Inherited Land Here
paragraphs: If your family sold surface land near Level Green decades ago but reserved minerals, that interest is still legally yours today even if you've never set foot in the current neighborhood. We help confirm and document that ownership before discussing what it might be worth.

faqs.question: My family sold the farm that became a Level Green subdivision — could we still own minerals there?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the original sale deed reserved oil and gas rights, which was common practice for many mid-century Westmoreland County farm sales.

faqs.question: Can a well actually reach gas under a developed subdivision?
faqs.answer: Yes — modern horizontal drilling can extend a wellbore thousands of feet from a pad set on nearby open ground to reach minerals under residential areas.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my family's old sale deed reserved minerals?
faqs.answer: We pull the original conveyance from the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg and read the reservation language directly.
